faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Our Services
faq.desc: Transparency is our foundational pillar. Discover answers to common questions regarding qualifications, placement fee structures, and legal protections.
faq.contactCardDesc: Our placement advisory team is ready to provide free in-person or online consultations.
faq.q1: What are the general requirements to apply as an overseas workforce candidate?
faq.a1: Candidates must meet core criteria: Indonesian Citizen aged 18–35 (subject to position specifications), possessing a valid e-KTP, Family Card, Birth Certificate, educational certificate (minimum Middle/High School/Vocational or Diploma/Bachelor's degree for skilled roles), notarized family/spousal permission letter, and physically & mentally certified fit through accredited clinical laboratory examinations.
faq.q2: What are the regulations regarding placement costs (Cost Structure)?
faq.a2: PT Amal Ichwan Arindo strictly complies with BP2MI Regulation No. 09/2020 on Placement Fee Exemption for designated sectors (Zero Cost) alongside government-approved statutory cost structures for formal/skilled roles. Full cost breakdowns (airfare, visa, training, medical tests) are transparently disclosed upfront with zero unlawful salary deductions.
faq.q3: What legal protections are provided for workers stationed abroad?
faq.a3: Every placement is safeguarded by three institutional protection layers: (1) Bilateral legal protection through verified Employment Agreements attested by local Indonesian Embassy/Consulate Labor Attachés; (2) Social security coverage through BPJS Migrant Worker programs and local destination insurance policies; and (3) Continuous monitoring by our accredited overseas partner offices.
faq.q4: What is the procedure for handling workplace grievances or disputes?
faq.a4: We maintain a dedicated 24-hour Case & Advocacy Helpdesk. Workers or their families can file reports through verified hotlines. Our overseas liaison teams immediately investigate with employers, convene tripartite mediation alongside Embassy representatives if necessary, and ensure all financial and worker safety entitlements are upheld.
faq.q5: What is the estimated timeline from screening to overseas departure?
faq.a5: Timelines vary depending on placement schemes and destination countries. For Japan's Specified Skilled Worker (SSW) track, it averages 3–6 months (including language training and trade proficiency exams). For formal manufacturing/construction placements in the Middle East and Southeast Asia, it typically takes 2–3 months following immigration calling visa clearance.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Destination Countries
faq.desc: Understand your legal rights and regulatory protections before submitting your overseas placement application.
faq.q1: How can I ensure the issued visa is an official work visa and not a tourist visa?
faq.a1: All candidates deployed by PT Amal Ichwan Arindo receive authentic employment visas (Work Permit, Specified Skilled Worker Visa, or Zezwolenie Typ A) issued officially by destination embassies in Jakarta. Authenticity is digitally verifiable on international passport systems and verified with BP2MI e-PMI databases before departure at international airports.
faq.q2: Are there zero-fee placement programs available?
faq.a2: Yes. In accordance with BP2MI Regulation No. 9/2020 and special bilateral arrangements (such as Saudi SPSK and specific sectors in Taiwan and Japan), primary costs including departure airfare, visa fees, insurance, and medical checkups are borne entirely by the employer. Cost structures are transparently disclosed prior to agreement signing.
faq.q3: What happens if there are workplace disputes or wage conflicts overseas?
faq.a3: Workers are protected by three layers of defense: legally binding Employment Agreements, continuous support from PT Amal Ichwan Arindo's overseas partner agencies, and diplomatic intervention by Indonesian Embassy Labor Attaches. We provide 24-hour emergency helplines to address candidate concerns.
faq.q4: Is language training mandatory before deployment?
faq.a4: Yes, for destinations like Japan and Taiwan, language certification (such as JLPT/JFT-Basic for Japan, and vocational terminology for Taiwan) is a mandatory regulatory requirement. Comprehensive curricula are conducted at our accredited vocational training center by certified instructors.

content.facilityTitle: Precision Science Industrial Park — Hsinchu & Taichung Hub
content.facilityDesc: Cleanroom work environment certified to ISO 9001 & ISO 14001, automated 22°C climate control, HEPA filtration systems, and international occupational safety protocols.
content.descP1: PT Amal Ichwan Arindo collaborates directly with leading electronic component manufacturing consortia in Taiwan to provide formal employment opportunities for skilled Indonesian talent. This role centers on operating precision assembly lines, printed circuit board (PCB) monitoring, micro-component insertion, and automated optical inspection (AOI).
content.descP2: Workers receive thorough training on modern industrial machinery, factory-standard technical Mandarin (conducted prior to departure at BLK Amal Ichwan Arindo), and professional workplace etiquette during a 1-month induction prior to assembly line commissioning.
content.task1Desc: Feeding micro-components into automated feeders, mitigating feeder jams, and preserving unbroken production flow.
content.task2Desc: Verifying solder accuracy, component pin defects, and circuit polarities via high-magnification microscopes and AOI display terminals.
content.task3Desc: Logging shift yield numbers, categorizing defect/reject components, and entering barcode metrics into production workstation terminals.
content.task4Title: Workplace Health & Safety & ESD Protocol Compliance
content.task4Desc: Wearing antistatic cleanroom gowns, grounding straps, particle masks, and adhering strictly to 5S industrial housekeeping principles.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions — Taiwan Corridor
faq.desc: Understand your employment rights, salary structures, immigration laws, and consular protections prior to signing legal contracts.
faq.q1: Is the NT$ 27,470 salary net or subject to statutory deductions?
faq.a1: NT$ 27,470 is the official gross basic salary adhering to current statutory Taiwan minimum wage standards. Lawful deductions include National Health Insurance (NHI ~NT$ 426), Labor Insurance (~NT$ 600), and dormitory/meal fees (capped at NT$ 2,500 - 3,500/month). Workers earn additional income through regulated overtime (OT).
faq.q2: What if I do not speak any Mandarin yet?
faq.a2: No prior knowledge required. All shortlisted candidates receive structured industrial manufacturing Mandarin instruction at PT Amal Ichwan Arindo's training center, covering machine nomenclature, cleanroom safety instructions, and daily conversation.
faq.q3: Is return repatriation guaranteed upon contract completion?
faq.a3: Yes. Under statutory Placement Agreements and Employment Contracts authorized by the Indonesian MoHR and Taiwan Ministry of Labor, employers are legally obligated to provide return flight tickets to Indonesia upon contract fulfillment, unless mutually renewed.
faq.q4: Who advocates for my rights if a labor dispute arises in Taiwan?
faq.a4: Official migrant workers are protected by the Indonesian Economic and Trade Office (KDEI) in Taipei and the Taiwan 1955 Foreign Worker Protection Helpline (toll-free in Indonesian). Partner agencies maintain on-site field staff for grievance mediation and assistance.
faq.q5: How long is the timeline from registration to airport departure?
faq.a5: Generally 2 to 2.5 months. This window encompasses Taiwan visa approval, TETO Jakarta authentication, vocational training, final medical clearances, and biometric registration on SISKOP2MI.
faq.q6: Are original passports or personal certificates withheld during employment?
faq.a6: Strictly not. Withholding original identity documents or passports is an illegal violation under both Taiwanese law and Indonesian BP2MI regulations. Passports, Alien Resident Certificates (ARC), and bank books remain in the worker's sole personal custody.
